subject: ACME Data Labs — degraded tail latency and client impact
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmedata.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: platform@acmedata.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 15:18:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden increase in tail latency — affecting downstream jobs

Hi Soojin,

We're seeing a sharp increase in tail latency (95th/99th) from the Hosted API starting ~14:50 PDT. Our background ingestion jobs are timing out and two internal customers reported failed invoice processing. Sample request IDs: rQ7a1, rQ7a4, rQ7b2 — those are returning 503 after long waits. Error rate has climbed from ~0.2% to ~3.8% around the window.

Can you confirm whether anything changed on the hosted side? We rely on the low tail latency for several synchronous flows. Please advise ETA for mitigation and whether we should failover to a cached path.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Platform Engineering — ACME Data Labs

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmedata.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 15:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden increase in tail latency — affecting downstream jobs

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the heads up and the request IDs. I'm escalating immediately to our on-call SRE and engineering leads.

Next steps:
- I'm looping in Markus (runtime lead) and Marissa (SRE) to triage; they'll confirm root cause and a short-term mitigation.
- Can you forward any Grafana snapshots or the request traces for those IDs if available? That will speed root-cause analysis.
- We'll follow up with a status page entry within 30 minutes and confirm whether traffic should be routed to a fallback.

I'll be your primary point of contact; will update as soon as I have an action.

— Soojin
Client Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 15:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden increase in tail latency — affecting downstream jobs

FYI — initial triage notes from the runtime team:
- Around 14:45 PDT we rolled a micro-release of a quantization kernel selection optimization to the hosted fleet (canary -> 40% -> 100%).
- We are seeing longer-than-expected stall times during KV cache warming under certain sequence-length distributions. That increases per-request latency for some infrequent large-context calls, which explains the spike in tail latency and the 503s due to upstream request timeouts.

Immediate mitigation plan (in progress):
1) Abort/roll back the optimization cluster rollout (Marissa to confirm and execute).
2) Move high-latency customer traffic to a stable model variant (traffic steering rule) for the next 2 hours.
3) Increase warm pool and pre-warm strategy for instances handling large contexts.

I'll own the postmortem and the fix path (kernel selection guardrails + more deterministic warming). ETA for rollback + traffic steering: ~20 minutes.

-Markus
Lead, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 15:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden increase in tail latency — affecting downstream jobs

Rollback started at 15:47 PDT. Observed behaviour: the canary rollout bump coincides with a small number of workers hitting eviction/warmup thrash which causes long-tail queues. Rollback to previous kernel selection profile in progress (deployment id: canary-quant-20270412-v2 -> reverted).

Telemetry snapshot attached (sample): telemetry-sample.log
Config we rolled back: rollout-config.yml

Current status: p95/p99 for affected clusters trending down; error rate falling. Will confirm in 10 minutes and post to the status page.

Attachment: telemetry-sample.log (text/plain)
Attachment: rollout-config.yml (text/yaml)

-Marissa (SRE)

Subject: Re: Sudden increase in tail latency — affecting downstream jobs

Hi Sanjay — glad to hear things are stabilizing. We're preparing a short status page entry and a post-incident report. Draft status blurb below — please let me know if you'd like any edits before we publish: 

"We experienced increased tail latency affecting a subset of Hosted API requests between 14:45–15:55 PDT on 2027-04-12. The issue was caused by an optimization rollout that interacted poorly with our cache-warming path. We rolled back the change and applied traffic-steering to stable variants; service performance returned to normal by ~15:55 PDT. We will publish a full post-incident report by EOD tomorrow with remediation actions and customer impact metrics."

Action items:
- I'll post the status page update (draft attached: statuspage-draft.md).
- Markus will own the postmortem and share a timeline + technical root cause.
- Laura (CS) will coordinate credit/remediation conversation; Soojin will keep ACME informed.

We will keep you posted and open a formal support case for credit discussions.

Best,
